scope: Finite abstract state-machine counterexample for hypothetical first-candidate contest rules. Replays saved Core headers locally; performs no new Core transaction, ZK proof, signature admission, payout enforcement or miner test. This is not an exploit of the existing storage graph, which has no fork contest.
assumptions: All compared branch headers pass the existing local HeaderChain validator.
Every candidate is assumed delivered and authenticated to the hypothetical contract before the submission deadline; that contract mechanism is still absent.
The provider may respond with the validated extension of its original tip before the response deadline.
Payouts occur only after both windows; no censorship or early payout is needed for the counterexample.

counterexample.action: reject: public challenge slot already consumed

counterexample.event: close submission window and finish response window

requiredInvariant: An earlier weaker or rebutted candidate must not permanently exclude a timely stronger candidate; merely delaying the final payout is insufficient.
missing: Provider response linked to the actual frozen candidate set
A bounded transaction graph supporting the required adversarial update order
Fixed payout, replay binding, fee and timeout enforcement
strongestCandidateAbstraction: A finite comparison oracle illustrates the missing invariant only. It is not a proposed implemented max-register, does not establish safety for arbitrary schedules or branches, and does not solve the presigned-parent or unknown-input binding problems.
